A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CityNav dataset and navigation models. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and rendered figures, support reliable comparison across renaming and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original navigation experiments, training-size comparisons, map-channel ablations and difficulty analyses in Section 4 and the supplementary material.

after.justification: v2 retains original navigation results and adds MapSeq2Seq experiments, GNSS-noise and disaster evaluations, and analysis of collected human trajectories.

M1.justification: Appendix D introduces MapSeq2Seq by adding navigation maps to Seq2Seq, a limited procedural adaptation. The core MGP pipeline remains: v2's retained MGP corresponds to v1's MGP+LLaVA, rather than introducing a new refinement method.

E1.justification: The CityNav corpus remains 32,637 trajectories covering 5,850 objects. However, v2 substantially extends evaluation conditions beyond normal city navigation to unreliable GNSS, flood inundation and earthquake-induced ground fissures across the evaluation splits (Tables 6 and 12).

E2.justification: v2 adds the evaluated MapSeq2Seq variant in Table 11 and removes the separate MGP-without-LLaVA comparison rows from Tables 2 and 3. Random, Seq2Seq, CMA and Human remain; the retained MGP rows match v1's MGP+LLaVA.

E3.justification: New evaluation protocols introduce test-time Gaussian pose noise, described as ±100 m, and training on normal scenes followed by testing in disaster environments. The reported training-size study contracts from 1k/8k/22k to 8k/22k trajectories. Existing splits, navigation metrics and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial robustness testing under pose corruption and altered terrain, tests whether human demonstrations also benefit MapSeq2Seq, and analyzes flight altitude versus distance to goal. It removes the comparison isolating LLaVA refinement and the 1k training-size conditions. Existing map-channel ablations and difficulty analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or performance error bars. The new altitude plot supplies descriptive means without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Tables 6, 11 and 12 report substantial additional results: for example, test-unseen SR is 3.27%/4.59% for MapSeq2Seq trained with SP/HD and 2.10%/5.42% for MGP under GNSS noise. Object-type percentages and altitude findings are also added. Matched retained scores are unchanged, including 6.38% test SR for v1's MGP+LLaVA with HD and v2's MGP with HD. Unrefined-MGP and 1k-training result entries disappear.

T1.justification: The Seq2Seq/CMA embedding, attention and recurrent equations, and MGP goal/progress definitions are retained. No new theorem, proof, derivation or substantive mathematical revision appears.

C1.justification: The dataset and map-based navigation contributions remain central. v2 extends the abstract, introduction and conclusion to claim robustness under challenging conditions, and elevates the already reported human–model performance gap into an explicit abstract finding.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly attributes reduced GNSS sensitivity to the diversity of human demonstrations. Appendix B interprets human trajectories as flying above buildings and descending near goals. The conclusion additionally specifies that stationary-building interactions were not actively considered because of the underlying city scans.

D1.justification: v2 documents test-time noise injection and normal-scene training for the new disaster evaluations, although simulation construction remains underspecified. It omits v1's statement that entity-name extraction uses few-shot prompting. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, map-caching instructions and dataset/code access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning VLN surveys, GRUs, search and rescue, GPS spoofing, OpenEQA and BEHAVIOR. It expands positioning around high-level instructions and practical applications, reclassifies AVDN's instructions from Dialog to Fine in Table 1, and changes CMA attribution to AerialVLN. The principal positioning against satellite imagery and game-engine environments remains.

P1.justification: Extensive paragraph-level rewriting spans the abstract, introduction, related work, dataset description, experiments and model appendix. The contribution list is reorganized, the supplement becomes lettered appendices, and terminology, citation style and affiliation text change.

P2.justification: v2 adds disaster illustrations and an altitude chart (Figures 6, 9 and 11), adds Tables 6, 11 and 12, and shortens Tables 2–4. A different typography and header template and widespread float relocation substantially revise presentation. Existing interface, model and navigation-example figures are retained across renumbering.

improvement.justification: MapSeq2Seq results extend evidence for human-demonstration benefits beyond MGP, while the new GNSS and disaster tests reveal behavior under previously untested conditions. These improve empirical assessment, but the gains are limited by underspecified simulations and comparisons using normal-condition baselines. Removing the unrefined-MGP and 1k results also reduces component and small-data diagnostic evidence.
